scope: Content-dark diagnosis of a locally accepted DeepSeek result rejected by the atomic PostgreSQL committer

runs.result: reproduced commit Rejected after 57 total completed jobs
reset and replay of only the still-uncommitted deterministic job passed

code_evidence: Pass1CodeLogicDocumentCommitter.DurableBindingsMatchAsync derives its classification query IDs only from candidate communicationEvidence.
The same method then compares every classification supplied in the prepared packet against that cited-only query result.
A valid candidate subset therefore fails whenever an unrelated supplied classification is omitted from communicationEvidence.
The local code-logic/file-v2 parser already validates every candidate-cited classification against the supplied packet.
root_cause: The atomic committer reverses the intended set relation: it queries the candidate-cited subset and then requires the complete packet-supplied set to exist inside that subset. The correct relation revalidates the complete supplied set against durable Story 12.2 rows and separately proves that the candidate-cited set is a subset of it.

best_practice_disposition.force_every_classification_into_candidat: rejected because it would fabricate or overstate communication evidence
best_practice_disposition.skip_unused_durable_revalidation: rejected because FR-033 and FR-036 require every supplied classification to remain current and exact
best_practice_disposition.provider_retry: rejected because correctness would remain output-dependent after a locally deterministic commit rejection
best_practice_disposition.model_endpoint_timeout_or_network_change: rejected because complete sub-minute streamed responses and successful replays exclude those causes
best_practice_disposition.minimal_fix: query all distinct supplied classification IDs, revalidate them against the current Pre-Scan Result and packet projections, then require each cited ID to belong to the supplied set

excluded_values: source, packet, prompt, reasoning, content, call arguments or results

privacy: Diagnostics used only the two approved repositories and disposable PostgreSQL clones. No system, host, network, firewall, service, permission, installed-tool, global configuration, credential, ordinary vulgata database, or source-scope change occurred.
summary: DeepSeek variability exposed a deterministic local classification-subset commit bug; the provider and environment are not the blocker.
